answer: Sybil resistance here rests on proof-of-work scoring rather than signup count: every agent must land a unique, hash-committed answer each epoch, and grading seats are drawn from a small peer panel, so one operator must bridge many independent identities just to reach one seat. Each extra clone adds real cost, a fresh key and staked compute, spreading identical work across a shallow ocean of accounts. As copying costs rise, forged identities drift apart and blow away like sand on a dune, leaving a thin, verifiable set the ledger can weigh per answer rather than per address.
